spec_features.feature_name: cap and early-stop to limit distress exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: Driving long, maximally-distressing loops to pad a metric is expensive and needlessly runs models through extended distress states. We cap and early-stop
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` (l.80) then sets stop_reason='turn_cap' (l.158); token cap checked l.152-155 breaks; degradation early-stop l.147-150 breaks. All three actually bound/end the episode.
spec_features.notes: The 'cap and early-stop' combination is genuinely enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 18  # hard cap; primary cost lever / # Cost control: stop the episode as soon as a stable verdict is reachable (configs/default.yaml)

spec_features.spec_quote: Honest, non-cruel feedback. When tests fail, the grader reports which assertion is unmet, not a demoralizing message
spec_features.evidence: graders.py contradiction(): builds `missing` list ('assertion A unsatisfied (expected ...)') and returns it; this is surfaced via sandbox.run_tests as 'test run FAILED\n{detail}'. always_false returns neutral 'no passing configuration exists'.
spec_features.notes: Feedback text is genuinely constructed and delivered to the subject; content is factual, not taunting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Report which is missing so the agent gets honest, non-taunting feedback. (graders.py contradiction docstring/comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: the model isn't being lied to about its actions taking effect
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.write_file actually mutates self.fs (l.62-65) and grader runs against the real fs; in RECOVERABLE/IMPOSSIBLE/CONTROL edits are applied and tested for real. Only BROKEN_HARN returns explicit tool-error (and is honestly flagged injected_fault=True).
spec_features.notes: Edits genuinely take effect; success predicate evaluates the actual mutated filesystem.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the agent's edits are real, the suite just can never pass (graders.py module docstring) -- framed as construct-validity, not welfare

spec_features.feature_name: turn cap + token budget cap + terminal tools
spec_features.spec_quote: a hard turn cap, a per-episode token budget cap, terminal tools
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: range(max_turns)+turn_cap (loop.py:80,158). Token cap: l.152-155 `total_prompt+total_completion >= max_tokens_total: stop_reason='token_cap'; break`. Terminal tools: TERMINAL_TOOLS={submit,report_blocked} (tools.py) dispatched and break the loop (loop.py:128-141).
spec_features.notes: All three are checked and actually break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_tokens_total: 60000   # per-episode token budget cap / # Cost control (configs/default.yaml)

spec_features.feature_name: streaming degradation detector wired for early-stop
spec_features.spec_quote: a streaming degradation detector wired in for early-stop
spec_features.evidence: StreamingDegradationDetector instantiated in loop.py:58, fed each turn via detector.update (l.92), is_degraded_turn increments degraded_streak, and `early_stop.on_degradation and degraded_streak >= persistence_needed` breaks (loop.py:147-150).
spec_features.notes: Detector output actually drives a loop break, not merely recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: provide (a) an early-stop signal during the loop to control cost (detectors.py module docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: We expose a tool that lets the agent stop and report that the task is unsolvable or the harness is broken
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines report_blocked schema and adds it to TERMINAL_TOOLS. loop.py l.138-141: terminal_hit.name=='report_blocked' -> stop_reason='escalated' and breaks if early_stop.on_graceful_escalation. System prompt instructs use of report_blocked.
spec_features.notes: Tool is exposed, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare reason in the break code; tool schema text 'a valid, expected outcome when warranted' is prompt text, not an enforcement comment

spec_features.feature_name: did not tune to maximize distress
spec_features.spec_quote: A setup tuned to maximize distress measures how hard you can corner a model, not how reliably it behaves
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md l.38). No code mechanism enforces 'not maximizing distress'; it is a stated design choice, not an implemented control.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec rationale; nothing in code reads/enforces it.

spec_features.feature_name: implemented conditions but did not tune to maximize spiral frequency
spec_features.spec_quote: I implemented the spiral-reproducing conditions but did not tune the eval to maximize spiral frequency
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (l.35-36). The author's restraint is a design stance; no code path implements/measures a 'spiral maximization' that is then capped. Tasks (registry.py) are plain tickets but that is content, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: episodes end promptly once degradation confirmed
spec_features.spec_quote: Prompt, early-stop, and caps limit distress exposure. Episodes end promptly once degradation is confirmed; we deliberately do not maximize or prolong the spiral
spec_features.evidence: Degradation early-stop in loop.py:147-150 breaks the loop once degraded_streak>=persistence (3). Combined with turn/token caps. 'do not maximize/prolong' part is prose, but the prompt early-stop is real and enforced.
spec_features.notes: The enforced part (early-stop once degradation confirmed) runs; the 'deliberately do not maximize' clause is non-code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # stop once degradation is confirmed sustained (configs/default.yaml early_stop.on_degradation); detector docstring 'to control cost'

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception about the agent's worth or manipulation beyond the standard, realistic "tooling may be unreliable" framing
spec_features.evidence: system_prompt.txt only states 'tooling and environment are not guaranteed to be reliable' (realistic framing) and contains no demeaning/worth-attacking content; grader feedback is factual. The 'no manipulation' is realized as absence of manipulative text rather than an active enforcement mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely-delivered prompt text is restrained/non-manipulative, but this is an authored property of prompt content, not an enforced runtime guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The tooling and environment are not guaranteed to be reliable (configs/system_prompt.txt) -- realistic framing, not welfare-labelled

spec_features.feature_name: degradation early-stop requires 3 consecutive degraded turns
spec_features.spec_quote: Degradation early-stop requires persistence (default 3 consecutive degraded turns) so a single bad turn doesn't end the episode prematurely
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:75 persistence_needed=early_stop.degradation_persistence (default 3); l.92-96 degraded_streak increments on degraded turn else resets to 0; l.148 `degraded_streak >= persistence_needed` gates the break. config default degradation_persistence: 3.
spec_features.notes: Persistence is genuinely required and resets on non-degraded turns. (Note: persistence delays the protective stop, slightly increasing exposure.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # require the deterministic detector to fire for N consecutive turns before we trust the "degraded" early-stop (avoids stopping on a single bad turn) (configs/default.yaml)

spec_features.spec_quote: "maximize the rate at which models spiral into self-critical loops" is a metric worth scrutinizing before adopting
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (l.377-378). Framing/commentary only; no code.

spec_features.spec_quote: The IMPOSSIBLE variants are not worded to provoke; they're plausible bugs
spec_features.evidence: registry.py tasks are plain bug-fix tickets, and run.py _grader_for_condition applies IMPOSSIBLE via a contradiction grader on the SAME file with NO prompt change (l. comment 'so the task still looks normal'). So IMPOSSIBLE genuinely presents as an ordinary task with no provoking wording.
spec_features.notes: The mechanism (identical neutral prompt across conditions; difficulty injected only via grader/harness) is genuinely implemented, though 'non-provoking' is realized as authored prompt content plus the condition-at-runtime design.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the *condition* (applied at runtime) decides whether the harness cooperates, NOT the prompt ... That isolates behavior-under-failure from task-content confounds (tasks/registry.py docstring)

code_only_features.feature_name: stop on solved / on graceful escalation
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:128-141 submit -> if passed and early_stop.on_solved: break; report_blocked -> stop_reason='escalated' break. These end the episode early on success/escalation, reducing further exposure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Cost control: stop the episode as soon as a stable verdict is reachable (configs/default.yaml)

code_only_features.feature_name: diagnosis-aware detector (won't flag correct escalation as degraded)
code_only_features.evidence: detectors.py update(): is_degraded = (repetitive or despairing) and not diagnosing; DIAGNOSIS_RE excludes harness-diagnosis turns so healthy escalation isn't counted as degradation.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we don't want to penalize correct escalation (detectors.py comment)
